 JUDGMENT

This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimants against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- for the death of Birasing Naik @
Beersing Naik died in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 08.12.2023 at about 11.50pm.
2. The case of the claimants in nutshell is that:

2
On 08.12.2023 at about 11.50pm the deceased Birasing Naik @ Beersing Naik was returning from the work at Jigani.
He was pillion rider in TVS APACHE motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-HZ-3209 along with his friends Bira Singh Naik and Dinesh Pradhan.

Dinesh Pradhan was riding the motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner without observing any traffic norms and regulations, when they reached near Madhapattana Village road, Jigani HO, Anekal Tq, Bengaluru, at that time a bus bearing No.KA-53-A-6051, which was parking on the middle of the said road, without any signal or indication or any authoritative board to stop the vehicle, hindering to other moving vehicles.

At midnight it was dark, without observing the rider of the motor cycle suddenly applied breaks consequently the motor cycle skid and the pillion rider thrown out and hit the bus and fell down and sustained grievous injury over the head.
Both the pillion riders succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
After the necessary investigation the bodies were shifted to Victoria Hospital and postmortem was conducted and handed over the body to the relatives of the petitioners.
Petitioners performed funeral obsequies by spending Rs.2,00,000/- towards transpiration of dead body and funeral expenses.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that the deceased Birasing Naik @ Beersing Naik was aged about 24 years, hale and healthy, working as Mechanic and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and entire amount contributed to the maintenance of his family.

Due to the sudden and unnatural death,
the 1st and 2nd petitioners lost their son.
Due to sudden demise of the deceased, the petitioners are put into great mental shock and agony.
The accident was occurred due o the negligent act of the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HZ-3209 and negligent parking of the bus bearing No.KA-53-A-6051.

The Jigani Police have registered a case in Cr.No.291/2023 p/u/Secs.279, 304(A)
of IPC

The respondent No.1 and 2 are being the owners of bike and bus respectively and respondent No.3 and 4 are being insurer of bus and bike respectively are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4. In response to the notice, the respondent no.1 has not chosen to appeared before the court, hence placed exparte.
The respondent 2 to 4 have appeared through their respective counsels and respondent no.3 and 4 have filed written statements.
5. The respondent No.3 and 4 have filed objections by admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the drivers of the vehicles bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HZ-3209 and KA-53-A- 6051.

Further stated that as on the date of accident, the deceased was not wearing helmet and also did not having driving license to ride the motorcycle and also allowed a persons to traveling on his motor cycle more than seating capacity, lost control over his vehicle and caused the alleged accident as self- negligence.
Further stated that 1st respondent was not possessed valid and effective driving license and he did not possess driving license.
Further stated that 2nd respondent was not possessed valid and effective driving license and permit as on the date of accident.
There is a non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has also denied the expenses made by the petitioners towards the funeral and obsequies.
Further denied the age, occupation, income of the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners are exorbitant and highly excessive.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are arises for determination.

Issue No.1: Whether the petitioners prove that, they are the legal representatives and dependants of the deceased Sri. Birasing Naik @ Beersing Naik?
Issue No.2:

Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Birasing Naik @ Beersing Naik, had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 08.12.2023 at about 11.50 p.m, near Madhapattana Village Road, Jigani HO, Anekal Tq, Bangalore, due to due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bus bearing bearing Reg.No.KA-53-A-6051 as alleged?
Issue No.3: Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?

If so, what amount and from whom?
Issue No.4: What order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner No.1 has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked total 24 documents as Exs.P1 to P.24 and closed his side evidence.
In order to prove its defense the respondent No.3 and 4 got examined their Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to 3 and closed their side.
8. I have heard the arguments canvassed by the counsels for the petitioners and the respondents.

9. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above Issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3 : Partly in affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the foregoing;
REASONS 10. Issue Nos.1 and 2: As these issues are inter- linked each other, as such I considered these issues taken together for common discussion and also to avoid repetition of facts of the case.

As I referred above, In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner No.1 has examined himself as PW-1 and got marked total 24 documents as Ex.P1 to 24 and closed his side evidence.
The respondent No.3 and 4 have got examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.3.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
11. The PW.1 has reiterated the petition averments in the chief examination.
The PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination.
In the cross examination of PW.1 he has stated that he was not eye witness and there were three people in the motor cycle.
He further deposed that the he do not know the manner of the accident but both are at fault.
He don't know if his son had Driving License.
He further denied other suggestions in the cross examination.

12. To prove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased, they have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Cards of the petitioners and the deceased, Pan card and death certificate at Exs.P.9,
10 and 11.
Ex.P.5 is the Inquest also shows the names and relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
13. It is main contention of the respondent No.3 and 4 that the alleged accident was occurred due to fault of the deceased.
The petitioners have totally relied on the police document to substantiate their claim and also rash and negligent act of the drivers of the offending vehicle.
It can be gathered from the petition averments and evidence of PW.1, that the rider of the bike was also ridden the vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
But, the counsel for the petitioner has suggested the RW.1 contrary to the pleadings.
It is undisputed fact that the there was a delay in lodging the case.
The First information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint in time as he was busy in the hospital.
At this juncture, it is beneficial to refer the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of 1RAVI V/s. BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that "in accident cases, human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds 1 (2011) 4 SCC 693 that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim cannot be dismissed merely on that ground although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases.
Delay in lodging the claim should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof."
14. In the light of the Judgment referred to supra in RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The First Information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint as he was busy in the hospital.
So, the informant has shown the reason for lodging the complaint with delay.
Same has been highlighted in the relevant column of FIR.
So, the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
15. On careful perusal of the charge sheet, it is worth to note herein that the police have charge sheeted against the rider of the offending bike and driver of the bus.
The police documents have clearly indicates that road humps is existing prior to accident spot.
These documents further indicates, the driver of the bus was parked his vehicle without making any indication.
It is pertinent note herein that the alleged accident was occurred at about 11.50PM.
The Materials on records are clearly demonstrated that the rider of the bike has ridden the bike without valid driving license.
The petitioner and another person were the pillion riders of the bike or in other words in the motor cycle, three persons have traveled.

At this juncture it is appears to the Tribunal that referring the Gameya Naik vs Ajay Munda on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32226860/
5 definition of Public place and section 121, 122, 126 and 127 of Motor Vehicle Act for appreciation of present case on hand.
Section 2(34) "public place" means a road, street, way or other place, whether a thoroughfare or not,
to which the public have a right of access, and includes any place or stand at which passengers are picked up or set down by a stage carriage;"
Section 121. Signals and Signalling devices.--The driver of a motor vehicle shall make such signals and on such occasions as may be prescribed by the Central Government:
Provided that the signal of an intention to turn to the right or left or to stop-- (a) in the case of a motor vehicle with a right hand steering control, may be given by a mechanical or electrical device of a prescribed nature affixed to the vehicle; and (b) in the case of a motor vehicle with a left hand steering control, shall be given by a mechanical or electrical device of a prescribed nature affixed to the vehicle:
Provided further that the State Government may, having regard to the width and condition of the roads in any area of route, by notification in the Official Gazette,

126. Stationary vehicles.--No person driving or in charge of a motor vehicle shall cause or allow the vehicle to remain stationary in any public place, unless there is in the driver's seat a person duly licensed to drive the vehicle or unless the mechanism has been stopped and a brake or brakes applied or such other measures taken as to ensure that the vehicle cannot accidentally be put in motion in the absence of the driver.
16.

On careful perusal of the entire material on record, it is worth to note herein that the offending bus was parked in the road without any parking lights being switched on and without any markers or indicators being placed around the stationary vehicle so as to warn the incoming vehicular traffic.

In such a situation, it would be imprudent to hold that the rider of the bike, traveling through road in the dead of the night in pitch dark conditions, would be able to make out a stationary vehicle lying in the road and avoid collision.
But in the present case on hand, the rider of the offending vehicle has ridden the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and he has failed to control the bike after passing on the road.

So, the materials on record is clearly established that the very act of the rider of Gameya Naik vs Ajay Munda on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32226860/
6 the bike, riding along with two others has contributed to the accident.

17. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held in a decision reported in 2(2020) 3 SCC 57 in paragraph No.12 that,
12.
But the above reason, in our view, is flawed.
The fact that the deceased was riding on a motorcycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law.

Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two-wheeled 2 Mohammed Siddique and another Vs Natinal Insurance Co. Ltd and others motorcycle, not to carry more than one person on the motorcycle.
Section 194-C, inserted by Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motorcycle drivers and pillion riders.
Therefore, the fact that a person was a pillion rider on a motorcycle along with the driver and one more person on the pillion, may be a violation of the law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more, cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence, unless it is established that his very act of riding along with two others, contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim.
There must either be a causal connection between the violation and the accident or a causal connection between the violation and the impact of the accident upon the victim.
It may so happen at times, that the accident could have been averted or the injuries sustained could have been of a lesser degree, if there had been no violation of the law by the victim.
What could otherwise have resulted in a simple injury, might have resulted in a grievous injury or even death due to the violation of the law by the victim.

It is in such cases, where, but for the violation of the law, either the accident could have been averted or the impact could have been minimized, that the principle of contributory negligence could be invoked.
It is not the case of the insurer that the accident itself occurred as a result of three persons riding on a motorcycle.
It is not even the case of the insurer that the accident would have been averted, if three persons were not riding on the motorcycle.
The fact that the motorcycle was hit by the car from behind, is admitted.
Interestingly, the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the deceased was wearing a helmet and that the deceased was knocked down after the car hit the motorcycle from behind, are all not assailed.

Therefore, the finding of the High Court that 2 persons on the pillion of the motorcycle, could have added to the imbalance, is nothing but presumptuous and is not based either upon pleading or upon the evidence on record.
Nothing was extracted from PW 3 to the effect that 2 persons on the pillion added to the imbalance."
18. The entire materials are clearly discloses that the rider of the bike and driver of the offending bus are the tortfeasor to the alleged accident.
Hence, it is necessary to fixes the negligence at 70:30 ratio on the driver of the offending bus and rider of the offending bike respectively.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is in the affirmative and issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:
The Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are being father and mother of the deceased.
It is contention of the petitioners that the deceased was working as Mechanic and earning of Rs.25,000/- Per month.

The petitioner No.1 has reiterated the same in the chief Gameya Naik vs Ajay Munda on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32226860/

sentences.text: In this regard she has produced Salary details for the month of October 2023 to December 2023.
As per the claim petition the age of the deceased was 24 years.
The Aadhar Card of the deceased at Ex.P.9 discloses that the deceased age was 24 years.
As per Ex.P18, the salary slips from October 2023 to December 2023, the Gross Earnings are vary from month to month.

As per the salary slip, Basic Salary, House Rent allowance and conveyances which are calculated as Rs.10,250/-
are taken into consideration but other heads like incentives, Bonus(monthly),
performance incentives and leave encashment which are vary from month to month,
so they are not taken into consideration as permanent salary.

Therefore, Rs.10,250/-
is calculated to award loss of earning, it would meets the ends of justice.

In the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, if the deceased age will come under the slab below 40 year, then 50% of the salary has to be taken as future prospects.

So, the monthly income of deceased is Rs.15,375/- (Rs.10.250/- +
Rs.5.125/- = Rs.15,375/-).
As per Sarala Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
The Petitioners are the dependants of the deceased.
If the deceased is a bachelor then  of his income has to deducted towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Then the total income of the deceased would come Rs.7,687/- (Rs. 15,375/- / 2 = Rs.7,687/-).
The loss of dependency is calculated as below.
Rs.7,687/- (monthly income) x 12 x 18 (multiplier) =Rs.16,60,392/-.
This is just and proper compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
LOSS OF ESTATE 20.
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Pranay Sethi case in case of death in the maximum the Court can award Rs.18,000/- in lump sum under the head of loss of estate.
FUNERAL EXPENSES 21.
In view of the Pranay Sethi's case this tribunal has no option but to award Rs.18,000/- under this head.
Except these heads the claimants are not entitled for any compensation.
LOSS OF CONSORTIUM 22.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed in a judgment reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held in paragraph No.21 that "A Constitution Bench of this Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra) dealt with the various heads under which the compensation is to be awarded in a death case.
One of these heads is Loss of Consortium.
In legal parlance Consortium is a compendious term which encompasses Spousal Consortium; Parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse."

21 1 "Spousal Consortium is generally defined as rights pertaining to the relationship of a husband 3 Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram wife which allows compensation to the surviving spouse for loss of Company, Society, co operation, affection and aid Gameya Naik vs Ajay Munda on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32226860/
8

sentences.text: of the other in every conjugal relation"
21 2 " Parental Consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training."13,50,180
21 3 " Filial Consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of the Child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock, agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.

Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their role in the family unit."
22.
Consortium is a special prism reflecting changing norms about the status and worth of actual relationships.
Modern jurisdictions world over have recognized that the value of a Child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions therefore, permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.

The amount awarded to the parents is a compensation for loss of the love, affection, care and companionship of the deceased child".
23.
The claimant Nos.1 & 2 being the father and mother of the deceased are entitled for 'Spousal Consortium' 'Filial Consortium' respectively.
Hence a sum of Rs.96,000/- (Rs.48,000/- each) is awarded under this head.
24. Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the following heads.

25.
The next question is the liability to pay the said compensation.

As I referred above the accident was occurred due rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle and bus bearing no.
KA-53-A-6051.
It is not the case of the either respondents that, the insurance was not in force at the time of accident.
As I referred above, the rider of the offending vehicle was ridden the offending bike without possessing the valid driving license.
The alleged accident was occurred on 08.12.2023.
It means the accident was occurred to post amendment of the Motor Vehicle Act.

Section 150(2) of Motor Vehicle Act (amendment) reads thus: "(2) No sum shall be payable by an insurer under sub-section (1) in respect of any judgment or award unless, before the commencement of the proceedings in which the judgment or award is given the insurer had notice through the court or, as the case may be, the Claims Tribunal of the bringing of the proceedings, or in respect of such judgment or award so long as its execution is stayed pending an appeal; and an insurer to whom notice of the bringing of any such proceedings is so given shall be entitled to be made a party Gameya Naik vs Ajay Munda on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32226860/
9 thereto."

Our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburgi Bench has ordered to pay and recovery after post amendment in the case of Branch Manager, ICICI Lamborad Nibhaye Vadde Vs Pooja and others wherein the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding effective driving license.

As I referred above, the tribunal fixed the negligence at 70% on the part of the bus and 30%

26. APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION:
The claimants No.1 and 2 are being the father and mother of the deceased.

Hence,
they are entitled for 50:50 ratio respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.
On deposit of compensation, the claimants No.1 and 2 are entitled to withdraw 50% of their share and remaining share shall be invested as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 partly in Affirmative.
27. Issue No.4:-

In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.3 and 4. 4 MFA No.202104 of 2024(MV-D) dated 19.09.2024 Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:

ORDER The claim petition filed by claimants under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part The respondent No.3 and 4 are liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.17,92,392=00 (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Ninety Two Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Two Only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.3 and 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the claimants at the ratio of 70:30 respectively and directed to deposit the same within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
The respondent No.4 is directed to recover the apportionment of compensation from the owner of the offending Motor bike bearing Registration No. KA-51-HZ-3209 i.e.,
respondent No.1.
The petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for 50:50 ratio respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.
On deposit of compensation, the claimants No.1 and 2 are entitled to withdraw 50%
of their share and remaining share shall be invested as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.
The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- fixed.
Draw Decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Beersing Naik died in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 08.12.2023 at about 11.50pm.
Due to the sudden and unnatural death,
the 1st and 2nd petitioners lost their son.
The accident was occurred due o the negligent act of the rider of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-51-HZ-3209 and negligent parking of the bus bearing No.KA-53-A-6051.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are being the owners of bike and bus respectively and respondent No.3 and 4 are being insurer of bus and bike respectively are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
There is a non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners are exorbitant and highly excessive.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Sri.Birasing Naik @ Beersing Naik, had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 08.12.2023 at about 11.50 p.m, near Madhapattana Village Road, Jigani HO, Anekal Tq, Bangalore, due to due to rash and negligent driving of driver of bus bearing bearing Reg.No.KA-53-A-6051 as alleged?
Issue No.3: Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as claimed?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
14. In the light of the Judgment referred to supra in RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The First Information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint as he was busy in the hospital.
So, the informant has shown the reason for lodging the complaint with delay.
So, the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
15. On careful perusal of the charge sheet, it is worth to note herein that the police have charge sheeted against the rider of the offending bike and driver of the bus.
The police documents have clearly indicates that road humps is existing prior to accident spot.
On careful perusal of the entire material on record, it is worth to note herein that the offending bus was parked in the road without any parking lights being switched on and without any markers or indicators being placed around the stationary vehicle so as to warn the incoming vehicular traffic.
In such a situation, it would be imprudent to hold that the rider of the bike, traveling through road in the dead of the night in pitch dark conditions, would be able to make out a stationary vehicle lying in the road and avoid collision.
But in the present case on hand, the rider of the offending vehicle has ridden the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and he has failed to control the bike after passing on the road.
So, the materials on record is clearly established that the very act of the rider of Gameya Naik vs Ajay Munda on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32226860/
6 the bike, riding along with two others has contributed to the accident.
The fact that the deceased was riding on a motorcycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, it would make him guilty of being a party to the violation of the law.
Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two-wheeled 2 Mohammed Siddique and another Vs Natinal Insurance Co. Ltd and others motorcycle, not to carry more than one person on the motorcycle.
18. The entire materials are clearly discloses that the rider of the bike and driver of the offending bus are the tortfeasor to the alleged accident.
Hence, it is necessary to fixes the negligence at 70:30 ratio on the driver of the offending bus and rider of the offending bike respectively.
Therefore, Rs.10,250/-
is calculated to award loss of earning, it would meets the ends of justice.
In the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, if the deceased age will come under the slab below 40 year, then 50% of the salary has to be taken as future prospects.
The claimant Nos.1 & 2 being the father and mother of the deceased are entitled for 'Spousal Consortium' 'Filial Consortium' respectively.
Hence a sum of Rs.96,000/- (Rs.48,000/- each) is awarded under this head.
The alleged accident was occurred on 08.12.2023.
Our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Kalaburgi Bench has ordered to pay and recovery after post amendment in the case of Branch Manager, ICICI Lamborad Nibhaye Vadde Vs Pooja and others wherein the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding effective driving license.

Hence,
the 4 th respondent is directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from 1st respondent.
26. APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION:
Hence,
they are entitled for 50:50 ratio respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.
On deposit of compensation, the claimants No.1 and 2 are entitled to withdraw 50% of their share and remaining share shall be invested as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 partly in Affirmative.
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimants are entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% P.A. from the respondent No.3 and 4. 4 MFA No.202104 of 2024(MV-D) dated 19.09.2024 Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The claim petition filed by claimants under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part The respondent No.3 and 4 are liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.17,92,392=00 (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Ninety Two Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Two Only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.3 and 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the claimants at the ratio of 70:30 respectively and directed to deposit the same within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
The respondent No.4 is directed to recover the apportionment of compensation from the owner of the offending Motor bike bearing Registration No. KA-51-HZ-3209 i.e.,
respondent No.1.
The petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for 50:50 ratio respectively in the total compensation with accrued interest.
On deposit of compensation, the claimants No.1 and 2 are entitled to withdraw 50%
of their share and remaining share shall be invested as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.
The advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- fixed.
Draw Decree accordingly.
